title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The previous page set up 'Deuring categories': Z-linear (more generally A-linear) categories whose endomorphism rings D = End(X) are orders in division algebras E = D⊗K. Using the reduced norm N_red : D* → A*, Grothendieck builds a canonical determinant isomorphism det P ≃ A for invertible D-modules P. This works under three conditions: Pic(A) = 0, Φ ∩ A* = {1} and Φ·A* = K*, where Φ = N_red(E*). For A = Z with E not split at ∞, these conditions hold: reduced norms are positive, and Q*_{>0} ∩ {±1} = {1}. One then gets a canonical invertible object of the associated gerbe.

This page applies the theory to the basic example.

1. The category C. C is the category of (supersingular) elliptic curves over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, with Hom as Z-modules. The qualifier and the exact Hom convention are illegible.
2. Deuring's input. By Deuring, C is a strict Deuring category over Z. All End(E) are maximal orders in the definite quaternion algebra B_{p,∞}. B_{p,∞} is the quaternion field (in his words 'de degré 4', i.e. dimension 4) split at every place except p and ∞. Its class is the unique nontrivial 2-torsion element of Br(Q) ramified exactly at {p, ∞}.
3. The gerbe. Over Spec Z[1/p] the maximal order is Azumaya, since ∞ is not a point of Spec Z[1/p]. Hence C determines a gerbe G on Spec Z[1/p] with lien G_m, together with an invertible (weight-one) representation of rank 2. In modern terms this is a G_m-gerbe whose class is the class of B in Br(Z[1/p]) ≅ Z/2, together with a rank-2 twisted locally free sheaf realising it. The dual group of invertible objects is noted T.
4. Adelic fibre functor. Put A' = ∏_{ℓ≠p} Z_ℓ. A banalisation of C_{A'} is a trivialisation of the gerbe over A', i.e. a fibre functor on Rep(Ĝ_{A'}) with values in A'-modules. The model is the prime-to-p Tate module functor E ↦ ∏_ℓ T_ℓ E. One adds an isomorphism φ(T) ≅ A'(1) = ∏ Z_ℓ(1), modelled on the determinant of the Tate module, i.e. the Weil pairing.
5. Comparison. Such rigidified banalisations form a gerbe H_{A'} under the norm-one / determinant-rigidified group. The page breaks off asserting a canonical equivalence G_{A'} ≃ H_{A'}.
6. The invariant (next page). The comparison has an invariant in a torsor Π under H^1(A', μ_2) = ∏_ℓ Z_ℓ*/Z_ℓ*² (Z/2 for odd ℓ, (Z/2)² for ℓ = 2). It is defined modulo the image of H^1(Z[1/p], μ_2) ≅ Z/2 × Z/2, generated by √-1 and √p, under the localisation map ρ. This ambiguity can be killed by extra structure: a polarisation at ∞ and an 'orientation' at p.

Purpose. To exhibit an integral, non-neutral Tannakian-type gerbe (a 'motivic Galois gerbe') for supersingular elliptic curves. Its Brauer class is that of B_{p,∞}, and its adelic fibre functor is given by Tate modules with determinant fixed via the Weil pairing.
errors: 'ℓ ≠ p, ∞': ∞ is not a prime ℓ. The meaning (exclude p and the archimedean place) is clear and harmless.
'de degré 4': in modern terminology a quaternion algebra has degree 2 (dimension 4). This is only a terminological slip.
The identification on the first line (some torsor 'of natural ...' equals ℍ_ℓ) is too illegible to check.

The definition of C is partly illegible. The word 'supersingular' and the exact Hom convention ('mod ... composantes') cannot be read with certainty, but the Deuring statement only makes sense for supersingular curves.

The remaining claims check out: Br(Z[1/p]) has a unique nontrivial 2-torsion class ramified at {p, ∞}; H^1(Z[1/p], μ_2) = Z[1/p]*/squares ≅ Z/2 × Z/2 since Pic = 0; H^1(A', μ_2) = ∏ Z_ℓ*/Z_ℓ*²; the definite-quaternion conditions on reduced norms hold. The ℓ = 2 case requires the mod-8 analysis, which he flags in the margin of the next page.

ideas.what: Category of supersingular elliptic curves as a Z-linear category all of whose endomorphism rings are maximal orders in B_{p,∞}
ideas.modern_name: Deuring correspondence (categorical form: equivalence with rank-one projective modules over a maximal order)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring 1941; categorical equivalence later made explicit (Kohel 1996 thesis; Ribet; Waterhouse 1969 for isogeny classes over finite fields)

ideas.what: Attaching to such a category a gerbe on Spec Z[1/p] with lien G_m and a rank-2 invertible representation, whose class is the Brauer class of B_{p,∞}
ideas.modern_name: Non-neutral integral Tannakian gerbe / G_m-gerbe with rank-2 twisted sheaf realising a Brauer class
ideas.usually_credited_to: Giraud (non-abelian cohomology 1971), Saavedra Rivano (1972); twisted sheaves: Căldăraru, de Jong, Lieblich (2000s); supersingular motivic gerbes: Langlands–Rapoport 1987, Milne 1994
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's Brauer-group / gerbe ideas appear in 'Le groupe de Brauer' (Dix exposés) and via Giraud; this specific example unsure

ideas.what: Adelic fibre functor by prime-to-p Tate modules over A' = ∏_{ℓ≠p} Z_ℓ, rigidified by an isomorphism of the determinant with A'(1)
ideas.modern_name: Prime-to-p Tate module fibre functor with Weil-pairing (similitude) rigidification; the adelic description of supersingular points as B*\B̂*/Ô*
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Deuring/Eichler; adelic formulation Shimura, Deligne, Langlands–Rapoport, Kottwitz

ideas.what: Canonical determinant / invertible object via reduced norm when the norms of a definite quaternion algebra meet units trivially
ideas.modern_name: Reduced-norm determinant functor; positivity of reduced norm of definite quaternion algebras

ideas.what: Torsor invariant in ∏ Z_ℓ*/Z_ℓ*² modulo image of H^1(Z[1/p], μ_2) = ⟨-1, p⟩; ambiguity removed by a polarisation at ∞ and an orientation at p
ideas.modern_name: Local-global sign/orientation invariant of an adelic trivialisation of a gerbe (comparison of rigidifications modulo global μ_2-torsors)
ideas.usually_credited_to: No clear single attribution; related to orientation conventions in Shimura-variety/Rapoport–Zink theory

missed.claim: In 1965 Grothendieck treats the supersingular elliptic curves as a non-neutral Tannakian-type gerbe over Spec Z[1/p], banded by G_m, whose class is the Brauer class of B_{p,∞}. It comes with a fibre functor over ∏_{ℓ≠p} Z_ℓ given by Tate modules with determinant fixed by A'(1). This prefigures the 'pseudo-motivic Galois gerbe' and the gerbe-theoretic treatment of supersingular isogeny classes (Langlands–Rapoport 1987, Milne 1994, Kisin 2017). It does so integrally (an order over Z[1/p] rather than an algebra over Q), which the later literature mostly does rationally.
missed.quote: D'après Deuring, c'est une catégorie de Deuring (stricte sur Z) ... une gerbe G sur Spec Z[1/p] de lien ... G_m, + représentation inversible de ce dernier, de rang 2
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early, integral formulation of the Deuring correspondence as Tannakian/gerbe duality over Z[1/p]. That is relevant to integral motivic Galois gerbes and to structural accounts of the supersingular isogeny graph.

missed.claim: The comparison of the Deuring gerbe with the gerbe of determinant-rigidified adelic trivialisations produces an invariant in ∏ Z_ℓ*/Z_ℓ*² modulo ⟨-1, p⟩. It is to be killed by 'polarisation at ∞' and 'orientation at p'. This sign-level local-global bookkeeping is begun but not completed in the visible pages.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a precise μ_2-level invariant for integral rigidifications of the supersingular gerbe. Such fine sign/orientation data are usually suppressed in the literature, which works up to similitude or rationally.

deep.surprise_reason: Historically notable: a 1965 integral gerbe-theoretic reading of Deuring's theorem, with Tate-module fibre functors and Weil-pairing rigidification, anticipating Langlands–Rapoport/Milne-style gerbes. The individual mathematical facts are classical, though, and the μ_2 invariant is an unfinished computation, so a specialist would find it a nice prefiguration rather than a new theorem.
transcription_corrections: 'Le tenseur des jauges naturelles' is probably 'Le torseur des ... naturelles'; the image is too illegible to confirm.
'groupes quaternions de degré 4 (corps de quaternions)' likely reads 'corps de quaternions de degré 4 (corps de quaternions)' or similar; 'groupes' is doubtful.
'qui s'explicitent en tous les places' is likely 'qui se déploient (s'explicitent) en toutes les places'.
'Hom mod ses composantes ... de car p' likely refers to curves over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p (supersingular); the reading is uncertain.
'consignés' is uncertain; the sense is 'correspondent' or 'se décrivent'.
'la gerbe des vecteurs courants de A'(1)' is uncertain; possibly 'la gerbe des trivialisations (rigidifiées par) A'(1)'.
